plan.name: BEAGLE MIND RELAY
plan.intent: Make Beagle's TOML style guides (global at appdata root + project-local at repo base) render into an MCP-surfaced directive that ANY front end (goose, pi, OpenClaw, future) can pull, at session start, on file use, and on context fold/compaction — so every session carries the relevant doctrine inside a usable context window, with Beagle as the single source and no per-front-end reimplementation.

defect.statement: No MCP entry point exposes the Top-of-Mind directive. A front end that connects only to the Beagle MCP cannot obtain the rendered doctrine.
defect.evidence: mcp_beagle_server.py has no style-guide/top-of-mind tool; grep for "style_guide|top_of_mind|render_hints" in that file returns only the _absorb tool mechanics. mcp_utility_server.py exposes only list_style_guides/get_style_guide (raw guide text), not the composed directive.
defect.mitigation: P1 — add tool `beagle_context_directive(scope_dir, phase)` + resource `beagle://top-of-mind` to the unified surface.

defect.statement: Delivery is goose-specific: the tom platform extension + GOOSE_MOIM_MESSAGE_FILE is the only automatic path; pi/OpenClaw get nothing.
defect.evidence: ~/.config/goose/config.yaml: extensions.tom enabled=true, GOOSE_MOIM_MESSAGE_FILE=.../beagle_top_of_mind.xml. No equivalent outside goose.
defect.mitigation: P2/P4 — front-end-agnostic injection at the three generic points (start, fold, file); goose keeps its path unchanged.

defect.statement: Per-session refresh exists, per-TURN refresh does not: the mounted beagle-context-management plugin fires render only on SessionStart (force=True); a mid-session style-guide edit drifts the TOML from the running session until the next session starts.
defect.evidence: hooks.json (beagle-context-management) registers SessionStart → beagle_bootstrap.py, which force-renders (beagle_bootstrap.py:412-420) ONCE; NO hook calls render-hints (grep "render-hints" in hooks/ + plugin = 0 hits). The goose-config-render dir at ~/.config/goose/plugins/ is a SEPARATE, NON-EMPTY, NON-mounted plugin (plugin.toml + render.toml + render_goose_config.py present, 3 entries) that renders beagle_system_instruction.xml — it does NOT refresh beagle_top_of_mind.xml. Correction of the DRAFT evidence: that dir is not empty, and beagle_top_of_mind.xml mtime = 2026-10-05 10:01 (fresh — auto-refreshed by the SessionStart force-render this session), NOT Sep 21. The residual defect is real but narrower: refresh cadence is per-session, not per-turn.
defect.mitigation: P4 — add a per-turn refresh path (UserPromptSubmit-hook or the render-hints --quiet call) so a mid-session TOML edit reaches the running session within one turn; the mtime-guarded render_canonical makes it cheap.

defect.statement: Compaction/fold rehydration carries no style-guide slice, so a front end that is not goose loses doctrine exactly when context pressure is highest.
defect.evidence: context/post_compaction_rehydration.py and infrastructure/tools/_impl.py own the fold sidecar; the sidecar content is task/progress, not doctrine. render_compact() exists (render.py:532) but nothing appends it to the fold payload.
defect.mitigation: P2 — fold tools append render_compact(domain) to the rehydration sidecar.

defect.statement: Three beagle working copies coexist; two are redundant, creating drift and "which one is canonical?" failures.
defect.evidence: `beagle` (MattCreigh/beagle @ cd11785), `beagle_dev` (MattCreigh/beagle_dev @ e5d29c96, 12 dirty files), `beagle-fork` (MattCreigh/beagle @ a8dacc6). `git merge-base --is-ancestor a8dacc6 cd11785` → 0 (a8dacc6 is an ancestor of cd11785).
defect.mitigation: P6 — keep `beagle`; delete `beagle-fork` (reversion-path: ancestor of pushed main); settle `beagle_dev` by fold-or-abandon decision (its diff touches ToM surfaces).

defect.statement: Project-local guide discovery is name-keyed (`<DIRNAME_UPPER>_STYLE_GUIDE.toml`) and undocumented to front ends; a repo without the exact filename silently gets no project doctrine.
defect.mitigation: P3 — document the convention in the session-start directive; add a `beagle_context_directive` coverage field listing resolved global+local layers so the absence is visible, not silent (HS-BOUND-01: typed absence, not None).

defect.statement: No conformance test proves the composed directive is identical across front ends (goose XML vs mcp_resource payload vs future adapter).
defect.evidence: targets/mcp_target.py returns a status string only; no cross-target equivalence assertion exists.
defect.mitigation: P5 — differential-oracle test (HS-EVID-01): same scope → byte-identical doctrine body across goosehints / top_of_mind_xml / mcp_resource.

claim.text: Global guide root is resolved by a single ordered strategy chain.
claim.cite: Resolution order for CONFIG_ROOT: 1. $BEAGLE_CONFIG_ROOT env var 2. ~/.config/beagle 3. <repo_root>/config 4. ~/.config/beagle (unpopulated).
claim.use: P3 renders global guides into ~/.config/beagle/style_guides/guides/; the directive reads the same root so there is one global SSOT.

claim.text: Project-local guides are discovered by walking up from the target path.
claim.cite: def discover_local(self, target: Path) -> list[tuple[Path, dict]]: Find repo-local ``[DIR]_STYLE_GUIDE.toml`` files above *target*.
claim.use: P1 the tool takes scope_dir and calls discover_local(scope_dir) so project doctrine follows the directory the front end was initialised in.

claim.text: Layer precedence is total: central ext-matched first, then local farthest→nearest; nearest overrides.
claim.use: P1/P2 reuse inject_for_file unchanged; the directive is a composition of render(domain) + inject_for_file(path), never a re-implementation.

claim.text: A front-end target axis already exists and includes a payload (non-file) target.
claim.cite: Return rendered content as a payload, writing no file. ... It is the mechanism by which OpenClaw (or later a `pi` front end) can pull directives over MCP. Pure and offline.
claim.use: P1 the MCP tool calls renderer.emit("mcp_resource", content, options) — no new rendering logic, satisfying PLG-5 / HS-BOUND-04.

claim.text: The renderer is pure/offline; the hydrator is the only network surface, with hard caps (8 KB hydrator, 25 KB doctrine).
claim.cite: v13.21: This module is the ONLY network-bound surface for the Top-of-Mind (Tom) XML. The renderer in ``render.py`` is pure (no I/O, no network).
claim.use: P1 the MCP tool stays pure; RAG/chat hydration stays in tom_hydrator so a stdio MCP call cannot create a network dependency (T4 fail-closed friendly).

claim.text: The unified MCP server absorbs core groups verbatim; adding a core tool needs no per-tool wiring.
claim.use: P1 adds the tool to mcp_utility_server.py (a core group) so it is absorbed automatically by build_app() (line 738).

claim.text: Raw guide access already exists as MCP tools, but not the composed directive.
claim.cite: async def list_style_guides() -> str; ... line 1509: async def get_style_guide(name: str, section: str = "") -> str
claim.use: P1 keeps get_style_guide (piece lookup) and adds beagle_context_directive (composed, scoped, phased). Distinct concerns, no overlap.

claim.text: The per-turn refresh entry point already exists and is failure-tolerant and mtime-guarded.
claim.cite: @render_app.command("render-hints") ... render_canonical is mtime-guarded and no-ops when the source TOMLs are unchanged
claim.use: P4 only needs to CALL it reliably per turn; no new render path.

claim.text: The render entry points needed by the plan already exist.
claim.cite: emit(...) line 823; render_canonical(...) line 870; render_compact(domain) line 532; render_all(...) line 2338; layers default ("global","directory","task") line 829.
claim.use: P1/P2/P3 compose these; no new renderer surface.
P6 deletion is reversion-safe (HS-MUT-01 / preserved-aside rule: pre-state is in pushed main).

claim.text: beagle_dev is a distinct repo with uncommitted ToM work.
claim.cite: git -C beagle_dev status --porcelain → modified .goosehints, CLAUDE.md, .goose/standards.md, src/beagle/context/rag_staleness.py, src/beagle/infrastructure/{cast_ingestion,delta_engine}.py, src/beagle/infrastructure/services/embedding.py, default_config style-guide beagle_core_directives.toml; untracked plans/beagle-pi-frontend-bundle.xml, qup.toml.
claim.use: P6 does NOT delete beagle_dev blind; it requires a fold-or-abandon decision and a pushed reversion path before any removal.

plan.legend: ENT(x) : x exists / is present RESOLVED(x) : x resolves through the single canonical resolver (no ad-hoc path) TOTAL(x) : x is defined for every input in its domain ⊨ : satisfies (green here implies the named property) ⊥ ↦ false : unevaluable predicate fails closed (deny) □P : safety — holds on every prefix (falsifiable by finite counterexample) ◇Q : liveness — eventually (needs a bounded-time drill, not a unit test)

phase.title: MCP surface — expose the composed directive

deliverables.item: mcp_utility_server.py: new tool `async def beagle_context_directive(scope_dir: str = "", phase: str = "session_start", file_path: str = "") -> str`.
Resource `beagle://top-of-mind` (FastMCP @mcp.resource) returning the session-start directive for cwd (declarative read for any client that prefers resources).
Response carries a resolved-layer manifest: {global_root, global_guides[], project_guides[], domain, bytes, cap_ok} so D6's absence is explicit.

phase.logic: EXIT_P1 ≡ ENT(tool.beagle_context_directive) ∧ ENT(resource.beagle://top-of-mind) ∧ RESOLVED(find_guides_dir) # one resolver, per C1 ∧ (∀ phase ∈ {session_start, fold, compact, file}, TOTAL(dispatch(phase))) ∧ (unknown phase → returns error string, never raises) # fail closed, T4 ∧ (bytes ≤ doctrine_cap) # 25 KB, C5

tests.test: tool listed by build_app(); resource URI present in app._resource_manager._resources.
phase=session_start in a py repo → directive contains python domain guide; in a repo dir with FOO_STYLE_GUIDE.toml → contains that local guide, ordered last.
phase with garbage string → error string, no exception; other tools still callable (process survival).
phase=file with a .py path == inject_for_file(path) byte-for-byte.

risks.risk: Importing style_guides into the utility server couples it to config resolution at import.
risks.mitigation: Import inside the handler (deferred), matching the existing lazy-import discipline (mcp_utility_server lines 44-99 tolerate a missing SDK).

phase.title: Generic injection points — start / fold / file / compact

deliverables.item: Fold path: in context/post_compaction_rehydration.py (and the fold tool in infrastructure/tools/_impl.py), append render_compact(domain=resolve_domain(cwd)) to the rehydration sidecar under a <doctrine_slice> element.
Session start: documented contract — front end calls beagle_context_directive(phase="session_start", scope_dir=<init dir>).
File use: file_discovery/code_context handlers may call inject_for_file(path) when a file is opened for edit (opt-in flag first).

phase.logic: EXIT_P2 ≡ (□(fold_fires → sidecar_contains(doctrine_slice))) # safety, testable ∧ (◇(sidecar_doctrine ≤ 8 KB over 100 folds)) # liveness, drill P-D2 ∧ (session_start path documented in the rendered hints + README) ∧ (file hook is off by default and cannot change existing tool return shapes)

tests.test: force a fold → sidecar has <doctrine_slice> with expected domain guide.
file hook disabled → file_discovery output identical to pre-change golden.

chaos_drills.drill: Run 100 consecutive folds in a session; assert sidecar doctrine block never exceeds 8 KB and never duplicates the full doctrine (§ liveness ◇).

phase.title: Default enablement — render on init, always-register

deliverables.item: Wheel post-install / `beagle init`: call render_all() so global guides land under ~/.config/beagle/style_guides/guides/ and per-repo pointers (.goosehints, .goose/standards.md, CLAUDE.md, .goose/project.json) are emitted for the init dir.
Document the project-guide filename convention (D6) in the session-start directive text and in docs/DOCTRINE.md.
MCP tools/resources always registered — no config boolean gates the surface (detection ≠ activation is preserved for PLUGINS, not for this core capability).

phase.logic: EXIT_P3 ≡ (fresh install → ENT(~/.config/beagle/style_guides/guides/*.toml)) ∧ (fresh clone + init → ENT(repo/.goosehints) ∧ ENT(repo/.goose/standards.md)) ∧ (no new required config key: grep for the tool's name in config TOMLs = 0) ∧ (idempotent: second init produces byte-identical files) # PLG-3

tests.test: clean venv + install wheel → global guides present; init in a sample repo → pointers present.

phase.title: Refresh hook + front-end adapters

deliverables.item: Per-turn refresh: add a UserPromptSubmit hook (or equivalent pre-read hook) to the mounted beagle-context-management plugin calling `beagle render-hints --quiet` so the tom extension's every-turn read of GOOSE_MOIM_MESSAGE_FILE sees the latest TOML. Note (D3 correction): the separate, non-mounted ~/.config/goose/plugins/ goose-config-render plugin renders beagle_system_instruction.xml, not the ToM — leave it out of this path.
pi adapter: pi's session-start hook calls the beagle MCP tool (or reads beagle://top-of-mind).
OpenClaw adapter: already the mcp_resource design target (C4) — document the one call.
Adapter contract file: docs/FRONTEND_CONTRACT.md — start / fold / file, nothing else required of a front end.

phase.logic: EXIT_P4 ≡ (goose: □(turn_n → top_of_mind.xml reflects latest TOML mtime)) # safety ∧ (◇(render-hints failure never breaks the turn)) # liveness, drill P-D1 ∧ (pi + openclaw documented against ONE contract, zero goose-specific branches in Beagle core) # HS-BOUND-04

chaos_drills.drill: Delete the dest XML mid-session, then issue a turn: render-hints recreates it; a corrupt source TOML must leave the previous artefact in place and exit 0.

tests.test: touch a guide TOML → next turn's beagle_top_of_mind.xml mtime advances and content changes.

phase.title: Cross-target conformance — differential oracle

deliverables.item: Test: for a fixed scope, the doctrine BODY of goosehints, top_of_mind_xml, and mcp_resource is byte-identical (only envelope/target-status differs).
Golden corpus: N ≥ 10³ (scope, phase) vectors → verdicts hashed; CI fails on any divergence (rule of three: 3/N bound).

phase.logic: EXIT_P5 ≡ (∀ target ∈ {goosehints, top_of_mind_xml, mcp_resource}, body(target, scope) = body(canonical, scope)) # HS-EVID-01 ∧ (0 divergence over the corpus) ∧ (corpus committed + replay harness in CI)

tests.test: differential oracle over the corpus → 0 mismatches.

phase.title: Repo hygiene — one beagle

deliverables.item: beagle-fork: delete after reversion path confirmed (C10 satisfies: ancestor of pushed origin/main). Record SHA in the removal commit message.
beagle_dev: decide fold-into-beagle vs abandon. If fold: cherry-pick the ToM-relevant diff onto a branch, push, then remove. If abandon: commit WIP to a pushed branch first. No uncommitted-to-delete.
Remove duplicate top-level skylon_plugin_{tailscale,vpn,wifi} only if skylon_ecosystem holds the canonical copies (separate check; out of P0-P5 scope, tracked as OQ-2).

phase.logic: EXIT_P6 ≡ (ENT(beagle) ∧ ¬ENT(beagle-fork)) ∧ (beagle_dev either folded (its diff pushed) or parked (WIP pushed)) ∧ (every removed path has a `git log --follow`-traceable pushed commit)

properties.safety: □ (same scope ⇒ identical doctrine body across targets). Falsifiable by a finite counterexample (one divergent vector).
□ (MCP tool call never raises into the transport; unknown inputs yield an error string). Falsifiable by one crash.
properties.liveness: ◇ (after a guide edit, the running session's next turn reflects it within one turn). Needs the bounded-time drill; a unit test cannot prove it.
◇ (fold doctrine slice stays ≤ cap across a long session).

verification.gate: static quality gate on every changed .py (lint/type/doctrine).
test runner for all suites; structured verdict gates phase success.
scripts/check_fail_closed.py, scripts/check_config_model_drift.py, scripts/check_no_editable_installs.py must stay green.
no new noqa suppressions (quality-ratchet: fix the input).
verification.install: uv build --wheel; uv pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps <wheel> --python /opt/beagle/beagle_venv/bin/python3; restart the Beagle extension (stale modules in running MCP servers).

rollback.step: Every phase lands on a branch `relay/Pn-<slug>`, committed and pushed before merge.
Config/render edits are idempotent and re-renderable from TOML (revert = restore TOML + re-run render_all).
The one destructive step (P6 deletions) is gated on a pushed commit; the removal commit names the reversion SHA.

open_questions.q: beagle_dev fold-or-abandon: which? (blocks P6; needs the owner's call on the beagle-pi-frontend-bundle.xml WIP).
Do the top-level skylon_plugin_{tailscale,vpn,wifi} dirs duplicate skylon_ecosystem copies? (out of scope for this plan; check before any removal).
Does the goose plugin API support a pre-read hook, or must the refresh be a scheduler entry? (determines P4 shape).
Should the resource expose the FULL doctrine or the domain-scoped slice by default? (default: scoped — bounded context is the point).
